newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks recoup some losses, Dow jumps over 100.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks recoup some losses, Dow jumps over 100.

text.p: U.S. blue chip stocks closed with sharp gains Monday as bargain hunters stepped in after the high drama of Friday's near record market plunge, sending the Dow up over 100 points.

The gains calmed many investors looking for signs of whether Friday's 250 point drop was the beginning of slower times ahead for Wall Street, or merely a temporary bull market correction after a phenomenal 1997 performance.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 109 points to 7803 unofficially, a gain of 1.4 percent.
"This was a very good first step," said Brad Weekes, managing director of equity trading at Donaldson, Lufkin Jenrette & Co.

A strong bond market, a stabilized dollar plus the underlying belief that the U.S. economy is still in good shape helped fuel the gains in stocks, he said. It also helped that that the market did not have to battle the double-witching expiration of futures.
The Dow started the session with gains of about 30 points before lurching lower to sharp losses as some investors switched into less-volatile bonds.

But bargain hunters emerged late in the session to take advantage of the low prices, driving the average to its high closing levels. But market analysts noted that, despite the gains, breadth remained negative. Stocks that fell outnumbered stocks that rose by a narrow margin, about 15 to 14.
Blue chips stocks fared better in the recovery than their smaller counterparts.
"We still have fears of slower corporate growth, but a lot of those big-name blue-chip stocks have fallen a good deal," said Scott Bleier, chief market strategist for Prime Charter Ltd.

Wall Street has lately begun to worry about whether one of the engines driving the bull market, strong corporate earnings, has begun to sputter after several profit warnings from high profile companies.
Today's earnings punch came from Hewlett-Packard Co, which reported disappointing third-quarter results due to slow sales of medical equipment and higher costs. Its shares slipped 2-3/4 to 63-5/16.
Consumer products stocks Gillette Co and Procter & Gamble Co continued to slide after Friday's news that Gillette Co expects slower profit growth.
Gillette fell 2-7/8 to 83 and Procter & Gamble lost 1-9/16 to 135.

Multinationals, drug stocks and other high-profile companies rose as investors stepped in to buy the stocks at such attractive low levels. General Electric surged 3-1/8 to 65-7/8, Merck and Co Inc rose 2-5/16 to 93-1/8 and Johnson & Johnson rose 2-1/8 to 58-1/16.

Wall Street was also trying to anticipate the outcome of Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting on interest rates, although most analysts believe the Fed will not move to change interest rates.
"The market's performance today was definitely encouraging because it implies we've had a a bull market correction -- they are short, sharp and furious," said Bleier.
In the downturn of the past two weeks, the Dow has given up about one-third of its gains from its April low of about 6,400 to its peak of about 8,300.
Monterey Resources Inc shares leaped 35 percent, adding 5-5/16 to 20-3/8 after the company agreed to be merge with Texaco Inc in a $1.4 billion stock swap deal.
Amylin Pharmaceuticals Inc shares lost 43 percent, hit hard by concerns over two of its Phase III diabetes drug trials. Shares closed down 6-7/16 to 8-7/16.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 7.49 to 1569.52.
The Standard & Poor's 500 Index rose 11.68 to 912.49.
((Wall Street Desk 212 859 1881))
